unit.title: Weather, Travel and the World Around Us

theory.title: Talking about journeys and transport
theory.explanation: Use by + transport to say how you travel: by train, by bus or by plane. Use take + a/the + noun for transport: take the train. Ask How much is a ticket? about price and How long does the journey take? about duration. Use the present simple for timetables: The train leaves at nine. Use comparatives such as faster than and cheaper than to compare ways of travelling.
theory.tip: Say by bus/by train, but on foot. Remember: How long? asks about time; How far? asks about distance.

content.passage: Mia and her brother are travelling to York on Saturday. They have return tickets and their train leaves at 09:40 from platform four. The journey takes about two hours. They arrive at the station early because they want to find the platform and buy a drink. Mia has a small backpack and her brother has a suitcase. Their train is on time, so they get on and find two seats together. When they arrive in York, they plan to take a bus to their hotel. They are excited because it is their first visit to the city.

content.audioTranscript: Good morning. This is an announcement for passengers travelling to Oxford. The train leaves from station two at nine fifteen. Please have your return ticket ready. Passengers for Bristol must change trains at Reading. The airport service leaves from the bus station, not the platform. The next bus is at six thirty. The 10:20 train is delayed by ten minutes. If you are travelling by coach, please check your departure gate. A train is usually faster than a coach, but tickets can be cheaper if you book early.
